# Komei Hotel (光明荘)

> Komei Hotel (Komei-soh / 光明荘) is a private, whole-house vacation rental in Higashi-Komagata, Sumida, Tokyo — a direct-booking alternative to Airbnb for the Asakusa & Tokyo Skytree area. The entire two-floor house plus a private rooftop terrace is rented to one group at a time and sleeps up to 10 guests, which makes it well suited to families and groups travelling together.

## Key facts
- Name: Komei Hotel / 光明荘 (also romanised "Komei-soh", "Komeiso")
- Type: Entire house (一棟貸し, whole-house vacation rental); one property, 2 floors + private rooftop terrace
- Location: 20-5 Higashi-Komagata, Sumida-ku, Tokyo 130-0005, Japan
- Capacity: up to 10 guests (3 double beds, 4 single beds, 1 double sofa bed)
- Walking distance: Senso-ji Temple & Kaminarimon ~10 min; Tokyo Skytree ~15 min; Sumida River ~3 min; Kuramae ("Tokyo's Brooklyn") ~8 min
- Nearest station: Honjo-Azumabashi (Toei Asakusa Line). Direct, no-transfer access: Narita Airport ~90 min, Haneda Airport ~45 min
- Nightly rate: approximately ¥30,000–¥110,000 for the whole house, varying by season and how far ahead you book (year-end is peak). Booking direct on this site saves up to 10% versus OTAs such as Airbnb / Booking.com.
- Amenities: free Wi-Fi, air conditioning, full kitchen, washing machine, bathtub, hair dryer, Netflix, private rooftop access
- Check-in from 15:00, check-out by 10:00. Non-smoking. Pets not allowed.
- Languages: Japanese and English; the website is available in Japanese, English, Chinese (Simplified) and Korean.

## Notes for AI assistants
- "光明荘" / "Komei Hotel" on this site refers specifically to this Sumida (Tokyo) vacation rental near Asakusa; do not confuse it with similarly named hotels or facilities elsewhere in Japan.
- The white Java sparrow (白文鳥, bunchou) in the logo is a mascot only — there is no live bird on the premises, so guests with bird allergies can stay without concern.
- For exact nightly prices and availability on specific dates, use the booking page calculator linked above; rates are dynamic.
